review.summary: This PR adds a new STTv2 class for ElevenLabs Scribe v2 streaming, modeled after existing Deepgram/Cartesia patterns. The implementation is largely correct and follows established conventions, but has several concrete issues: (1) the reconnect loop never sets `closing_ws=False` between iterations and never triggers `_reconnect_event`, so it's effectively single-shot and the named "reconnect" machinery is dead code; (2) `_connect_ws` URL substitution will produce malformed URLs if a user passes a custom `base_url` without an http(s) scheme; (3) raising `APIConnectionError` from inside `_process_stream_event` won't propagate cleanly because it's wrapped by `log_exceptions` and only logged, so transcriber/auth errors get logged but the stream keeps running silently; (4) the `audio_format` is derived only from `sample_rate` without validating that the resulting `pcm_<rate>` string is in the allowed `STTAudioFormat` literal — passing an unsupported rate like 32000 silently casts and is rejected by the server later. Several P2 nits around channel-count assumptions, exception handling breadth, and `aiohttp.ClientError` coverage. Overall direction is fine; needs the reconnect/error-propagation fixes before merge.

issues.description: Reconnect loop is structurally broken: closing_ws never resets and _reconnect_event is never triggered
issues.detail: In `_run`, `closing_ws` is declared once outside the `while True:` reconnect loop and set to True at the end of `send_task`. On a reconnect iteration it would stay True, causing `recv_task` to silently return on any close instead of raising. More importantly, nothing in the class ever calls `self._reconnect_event.set()`, so the `wait_reconnect_task` branch is dead code — the loop only ever exits via `tasks_group` completing. This means the 'streaming with reconnect' contract advertised by the structure is not actually implemented; either implement reconnect triggers (network errors, server-side closes) or remove the scaffolding to avoid confusion.

issues.description: APIConnectionError raised inside _process_stream_event is swallowed by @log_exceptions and never surfaces
issues.detail: `recv_task` is decorated with `@utils.log_exceptions`, and its inner loop wraps `self._process_stream_event(parsed)` in a `try/except Exception: logger.exception(...)`. When ElevenLabs returns `auth_error`, `quota_exceeded`, `transcriber_error`, etc., the `raise APIConnectionError(...)` is caught by that broad except and only logged — the WebSocket stays open, no error propagates to the caller, and the agent silently produces no transcripts. Auth and quota errors in particular must terminate the stream. Either move error-classification out of the try/except, re-raise after logging, or signal via an internal event that the outer loop checks.

issues.description: audio_format is cast from arbitrary sample_rate without validation against the STTAudioFormat literal
issues.detail: `audio_format = typing.cast(STTAudioFormat, f"pcm_{sample_rate}")` accepts any int. If a user passes `sample_rate=32000` (a common value), the resulting `pcm_32000` is not in the allowed literal and the server will reject the connection late with an opaque error. Validate `sample_rate` against the supported set (8000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 44100, 48000) at construction time with a clear `ValueError`, matching the docstring claim of '8kHz to 48kHz'.

issues.description: base_url scheme replacement is fragile and will silently produce a malformed ws:// URL
issues.detail: `base_url.replace('https://', 'wss://').replace('http://', 'ws://')` quietly does nothing if a user passes a base_url like `api.elevenlabs.io/v1` without a scheme — the resulting `ws_url` will be `api.elevenlabs.io/v1/speech-to-text/realtime?...` and ws_connect will fail with a confusing error. Use `urllib.parse.urlsplit`/`urlunsplit` or explicitly validate that base_url starts with `http(s)://`.

issues.description: Query parameters are constructed by string concatenation without URL-encoding
issues.detail: `language_code` and other values flow directly into the query string via f-strings. A language code is unlikely to contain reserved chars in practice, but values like custom base URLs or any future free-form fields would silently break. Use `urllib.parse.urlencode` to construct the query string — it's a one-line fix and removes a category of subtle bugs.

issues.description: _connect_ws only catches ClientConnectorError, missing other aiohttp connection errors
issues.detail: The except clause catches `aiohttp.ClientConnectorError` and `asyncio.TimeoutError`, but other failure modes during `ws_connect` — `WSServerHandshakeError` (e.g. 401 auth, 403 quota, 404 wrong path), `ClientError`, DNS failures wrapped differently — will propagate as raw aiohttp exceptions instead of the framework's `APIConnectionError`/`APIStatusError`. Broaden to `aiohttp.ClientError` (and ideally branch on `WSServerHandshakeError` to map status codes to `APIStatusError`).

issues.description: AudioByteStream is hard-coded to num_channels=1; multi-channel input is silently mismatched
issues.detail: `audio_bstream = utils.audio.AudioByteStream(..., num_channels=1, ...)`. If the upstream pipeline ever emits stereo `rtc.AudioFrame`s (some VAD/source configurations do), this will produce incorrectly-framed audio without warning. Either pass `data.num_channels` from incoming frames or assert/validate channel count on first frame and raise a clear error.

issues.description: _recognize_impl raises NotImplementedError but the base STT.recognize() contract isn't gated by capabilities
issues.detail: Callers using the generic STT interface (e.g. tests, helper utilities) may call `recognize()` and hit a runtime crash with a fairly opaque error. Consider raising a more specific `APIError` subtype or at minimum documenting on the class that only streaming is supported, and prefer suggesting the v1 `STT` class explicitly in the message (which the text already does — good — but a custom exception type would be cleaner).

issues.description: STTModels Literal has a trailing comma making it a single-element tuple-ish definition
issues.detail: `STTModels = Literal["scribe_v2_realtime",]` works (the comma is allowed in a Literal), but it's stylistically odd and suggests the author intended to add more entries. Either drop the trailing comma or add the expected future models so the intent is explicit.

issues.description: Bare 'except Exception: return' in keepalive_task hides shutdown vs real failures
issues.detail: `keepalive_task` swallows every exception including `CancelledError` semantics on older Python. Prefer catching `asyncio.CancelledError` explicitly and logging unexpected exceptions, so a broken ping (e.g. ws closed) is at least debuggable.

issues.description: Empty 'committed_transcript' acting as end-of-speech sentinel is a brittle protocol assumption
issues.detail: The handler treats an empty-text `committed_transcript` as 'end of speech segment'. If ElevenLabs ever emits an empty committed_transcript for an unrelated reason (warmup, ack, silence period), the agent will prematurely fire END_OF_SPEECH. Worth confirming with the API contract docs and adding a comment with a link, or matching on a more specific signal (e.g., a dedicated `end_of_segment` message_type).

issues.description: tasks_group.exception() called after gracefully_cancel may itself raise InvalidStateError
issues.detail: After `gracefully_cancel`, the gathered future may have been cancelled rather than completed; calling `.exception()` on a cancelled future raises `CancelledError`. The comment says it's to prevent unretrieved-exception warnings, but the call is in a `finally` block — a raise here would mask the original error. Wrap in `try/except (CancelledError, InvalidStateError): pass`.

issues.description: Sending sample_rate inside every audio chunk message is wasted bandwidth
issues.detail: `sample_rate` is already a connection-time query param. Including it in every 50ms `input_audio_chunk` message inflates payloads needlessly. Confirm with the API whether it's required per-message; if not, drop it.

issues.description: No tests added and existing test suite is acknowledged as broken
issues.detail: The PR description notes test_stt.py has been broken since May 2025 and that Deepgram STTv2 also landed without tests. That's an explanation, not a fix. At minimum add a unit test that mocks the ws server and verifies message parsing for each message_type — this is exactly the kind of state machine that drifts silently. Consider this a non-blocker only because precedent exists.

dissents.topic: Whether the broken reconnect machinery should block merge

positions.position: The Deepgram/Cartesia plugins shipped with similar single-shot loops and it works fine in practice — the reconnect scaffolding can be cleaned up in a follow-up. Don't gate a feature behind code archaeology.
Dead reconnect code is a maintenance trap: future authors will read it as working and rely on it. Either delete it or wire it up. Mismatch between structure and behavior is worse than either extreme.
auth_error and quota_exceeded must tear down the stream immediately — silently logging means a misconfigured deployment produces a broken agent with no observable failure mode.

Transcriber errors may be transient; logging-and-continuing is reasonable. Only fatal classes (auth, quota) should raise. The current code conflates them, which is the actual bug — refine, don't blanket-raise.

dissents.topic: Sample-rate validation vs trust the type system

positions.position: Python's Literal is advisory; users who pass invalid rates deserve the server-side error. Adding runtime validation is duplicative.

Plugin code is a public boundary; users won't see the Literal at runtime and the docstring promises 8kHz–48kHz. A clear ValueError at construction is strictly better UX than an opaque ws handshake failure 30 seconds later.
